summary.intent: Reduce disk usage and clutter in the caliper repo and surrounding projects (stale worktrees, huge .git, build targets), then design a sane plan for what lives where, naming, caching and cleanup.
summary.outcome: Worktrees under .claude/worktrees were cut from 68 to about 7 (65 GB to under 2 GB), about 60 GB of finished-job scratch and several GB of dormant target dirs were deleted, and #504 was merged. The .git size cause was diagnosed as Entire session logs, and a by-lifetime storage plan was proposed but not yet approved or implemented.

repo: Worktrees share one object store, so shallow or sparse checkout saves nothing; the disk cost is per-worktree `target/` (about 4-5 GB each, full debug info) and `node_modules` (about 400 MB, partly shared via pnpm).

The .git directory is 811 MB: 449 MB of objects plus a 296 MB `entire-redact-cache`. Of 266 MiB of blob data, 256 MiB is Entire session transcripts under refs/entire/checkpoints (2,585 refs), pushed to the public GitHub origin.
The largest transcripts are dominated by base64 screenshots, extracted PDF text and API request blobs. One contains reads of personal Desktop PDFs, which is a privacy concern on a public repo.
`entire clean` only touches session state and shadow branches; `entire checkpoint delete <id> --dry-run` removes a checkpoint locally and from checkpoint remotes.

Agent worktrees were locked by dead processes (pid 40549 and 44130), so they needed `git worktree unlock` before non-force `git worktree remove`. Non-force removal refuses worktrees with modified or untracked files, which acts as a safety net.
oxc-release-builds and oxc-stack are standalone clones with their own .git, not worktrees, so git cannot remove them. caliper-homebrew-tap was refused for dirty files.

Real corpora are fetched by `scripts/corpora.py setup` into `.corpora/repos` (gitignored); `weekly.py --corpora DIR` can override. In-repo `fixtures/` holds 23 small sample libraries (404 KB). Neither depends on the deleted caliper-fixtures directory.
`just test-checker-lane` hard-wires `$PWD/target/release`, which blocks a shared CARGO_TARGET_DIR.
Entire Gates showed 'Mergeable: no' on #504 solely because of the approvals gate, with all CI and findings gates passing.
Entire's outgoing checkpoints should be flushed (a no-op push worked) before removing a worktree.
workflow: Delegated subagents are pinned to their worktree and the Bash guard refuses `git -C <other path>` and compound git commands, so cross-worktree status surveys cannot run from them; run them from the main checkout.
Deleting from the CLI bypasses Trash, and APFS local snapshots then hold the freed space (df unchanged) until they expire or are thinned.
Use `$TMPDIR` for scratch, not a named directory outside the repo; a location should hold only what its name says (saved to memory as fixtures-is-not-scratch).
Remove a worktree and its `target` as soon as its PR merges; a documented cleanup routine fits the user's no-new-scripts rule.
Measure before proposing changes such as `debug = "line-tables-only"` or sccache.

friction: The caliper-fixtures directory was deleted via CLI mid-session, losing accept.sh, oracle reports, pattern-eval.md (the spec for changes 8, 7 and D) and corpora; only the worker contract was reconstructed to memory.
The subagent survey could not check dirty state because of the Bash guard, so removal decisions for eight dirty worktrees remained unresolved.
I miscounted worktrees (said 15, actually 14) and had to correct it.
Deleted data was still held by 22 Time Machine snapshots, so df showed no freed space.
Worker contract told every worker to dump build output into caliper-fixtures, creating around 90 per-task directories and GB of misnamed content.
gh needed the sandbox off because of a TLS check failure.
